title: City centres without cars
context_es: En clase habéis hablado de la vida en las ciudades. Tu profesor te pide un ensayo, como en la Parte 1 del Writing de B2 First.
prompt_en:
In your English class you have been talking about life in cities. Now your teacher has asked you to write an essay.

Some people think that cars should be banned from city centres. Do you agree?

Notes
Write about:
1. pollution
2. shops and businesses
3. your own idea
useful_language: In conclusion, I am convinced that …
tips_es: Estructura: introducción, un párrafo por nota (las dos dadas y la tuya) y conclusión con tu opinión.
Registro formal: sin contracciones ni exclamaciones, y con conectores (*However, In addition, Therefore*).
La tercera nota es tuya: elige una idea distinta de las otras dos y desarróllala igual.
model_answer:
Traffic is one of the biggest problems in modern cities, and some councils have decided to close their centres to private cars. Although this measure is controversial, I believe that it brings more benefits than disadvantages.

First of all, banning cars reduces pollution. Exhaust fumes are responsible for many health problems, especially among children and elderly people. When cars disappear, the air becomes cleaner and the streets are far quieter.

On the other hand, many shop owners fear that they will lose customers who cannot park nearby. Nevertheless, experience in cities such as Pontevedra shows that people spend more time, and more money, in streets where they can walk safely. In addition, deliveries can still be allowed early in the morning.

A further point is public space. A parked car occupies around ten square metres that could be used for trees, benches or playgrounds. As a result, the centre becomes a place to live in rather than a place to drive through.

In conclusion, although the change requires good public transport, I am convinced that city centres without cars are healthier, more attractive and better for business.
